transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jenna Cruz (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (CSM), Samir Patel (SE), Dr. Maya Singh (VantageCare CTO), Carlos Rios (Head Eng), Priya Kapoor (PM), Liam O'Neal (Security Lead)

Summary:
Redwood onboarding kickoff for VantageCare focusing on private deployment options (VPC), SSO/SAML, data residency and initial pilot benchmarks. Confirmed success criteria: sub-200ms token latencies for chat, PII-safe handling, and week-long perf run. Next steps and owners captured.

00:00 Jenna (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round intro 
I'm Jenna, I'll be your AE and point person for commercial stuff. Lena is your CSM, Samir will handle technical and bench tests. Maya, Carlos, Priya, Liam from VantageCare?
00:18 Dr. Maya Singh (VantageCare): Yep hi, Maya here. Thanks for setting this up. We're excited to get started on the pilot, want to make sure we get security and latency nailed down.
00:30 Carlos Rios: Carlos here. main constraint is we have an existing EHR pipeline, need inference to sit behind our VPC and ideally no data leaves region.
00:45 Jenna: Great, we'll walk through high level plan today and then dig into VPC and perf. quick note 
I'll send the onboarding deck and SSO steps after.
01:02 Samir (SE): Quick add 
we'll propose either Dedicated or Private depending on throughput and security needs. private gives you full VPC administration, Dedicated is isolated pools but managed by us. we'll propose a config for both.
01:25 Priya Kapoor: Timeline question 
is we want production in 6-8 weeks, is that feasible?
01:33 Lena (CSM): 6-8 weeks is doable for a pilot -> prod if there are no blockers on SSO and network. We usually see 2 weeks for infra setup, 1 week for integration, then 2-3 weeks of pilot and tuning.
01:50 Liam (Security): On compliance, we need SOC 2 report, encryption at rest and in transit, and support for customer-managed KMS. Also audit logs retention for 1 year.
02:05 Jenna: We have SOC 2, ISO references, and KMS integrations 
I'll attach our security pack. audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via S3 or direct splunk/stackdriver integration.
02:28 Dr. Maya Singh: Also need to check data residency 
all inference should stay in us-west-2. any issues?
02:40 Samir: That's fine. Private deployment can be inside your VPC in us-west-2 region. We'll confirm AMI/helm chart specifics in the follow-up doc.

05:00 Topics: VPC peering, SSO/SAML, KMS & encryption, performance benchmarks, pilot success criteria, rollout plan.

05:30 Carlos: Architecture note 
we currently run main services in EKS and have an internal API gateway. We want Redwood inference to sit behind our gateway with mTLS.
05:45 Samir: mTLS + private endpoints supported. we recommend a sidecar pattern or internal LB depending on latency. sidecar reduces network hops but needs kube changes.
06:05 Jenna: For scale, what's your expected peak qps?
06:12 Carlos: Ballpark 40 concurrent chat sessions during peak, 100 requests/minute, average prompt length 250 tokens, mostly chat use-cases.
06:28 Samir: That maps to modest Dedicated pool or single Private cluster with 2 GPU nodes; we'll size GPUs based on model choice. are you planning to use a larger open model or a smaller optimized one?
06:45 Priya: We're evaluating two things 
a higher-quality generative model for patient triage, and embeddings for semantic search. cost matters 
we want to control per-token costs.
07:00 Jenna: Redwood Optimize will help recommend quantization and batching settings. For embeddings we can use smaller models and cache vectors in your DB.

10:00 (transcription glitch) Speaker 2: ...and then, the 
billing side, um is that per-token plus reserved?
10:10 Jenna: Yes hosted is per-token. For Dedicated/Private there are reserved capacity contracts plus usage. I'll include pricing examples in the follow-up.

12:00 Security deep dive
12:10 Liam (Security): A few clarifying Qs 
does Redwood support customer-managed keys for disk encryption and for transit? we also need field-level PII redaction or a pattern for not sending PHI to inference.
12:30 Samir: We can integrate with your KMS/HSM for disk and envelope encryption. For PHI redaction we usually recommend a pre-processing step in your pipeline that strips or tokenizes PHI, or run inference in your private cluster so the data never leaves your network. we also have a redaction library we can share.
12:55 Priya: Can we run a classifier locally to mask fields, then send masked content for generation?
13:05 Samir: Absolutely. that's a common recommended approach. we'll share best-practice guide.

15:30 Performance discussion
15:40 Carlos: What's realistic latency for chat at our size? target sub-200ms per token is ideal.
15:52 Samir: sub-200ms per token is aggressive for larger models 
for smaller optimized models with quantization we can get close. with batching kernels and GPU optimized runtimes, steady-state token latency of ~80-150ms is reasonable depending on seq length and model. We'll run bench tests to validate.
16:20 Jenna: For the pilot, Samir will propose a model variant and run a 7-day perf window to show tail latencies and costs.

20:00 Questions from customer
20:10 Priya: Who will own the rollout tasks 
do we handle migrations or do you assist?
20:18 Lena: We'll work jointly: CSM coordinates, SE works on integration and benchmarks, and we'll provide runbooks and playbooks for migration.

24:00 Discussion about tooling and observability
24:12 Samir: Redwood Console will give you per-route latency and token cost breakdowns. we can set up tracing hooks to correlate your request IDs.
24:35 Carlos: Can logs be forwarded to our central logging?
24:42 Jenna: Yes, logs can be exported to S3 and pushed to your SIEM; retention configurable.

28:30 Pricing and licensing notes
28:40 Jenna: I'll include two pricing scenarios: Dedicated reserved monthly vs Private one-time deployment fee plus support. Will include example TCO with batching and caching savings.

33:00 Pilot success criteria (agreed)
33:10 Priya: 1) Latency under 250ms p50 and p95 under 600ms during pilot with our traffic. 2) No data exfiltration; KMS + VPC enforced. 3) Acceptance of accuracy level on our prompt set 
we'll define a small eval suite.
33:36 Lena: We'll instrument quality monitoring and set regression alerts tied to your prompt set.

36:00 Wrap and next steps
36:10 Jenna: Recap 
I'll send the onboarding deck + security pack + SSO guide. Samir will share test plan and schedule bench. Lena will create the project and invite your admins. Carlos to share network diagram and Liam to validate KMS requirements.
36:35 Carlos: Sounds good. we'll aim to have network details by Friday.
36:45 Dr. Maya Singh: One last ask 
can you include a short runbook for rollback if the pilot causes issues?
36:55 Samir: yes we'll add rollback steps and fallback policy (model variant fallback and routing to hosted) in the runbook.

40:00 Quick snags / clarifications
40:05 Priya: On embeddings 
can we index in our DB and have Redwood store only encrypted vectors?
40:15 Samir: vectors can be stored in your DB; we also support managed vector DB with encryption at rest if you prefer.

44:00 Close
44:05 Jenna: Thanks everyone 
we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
44:18 Meeting ended.

References mentioned: onboarding deck (link to share), security pack (link to SSO/KMS docs), benchmark plan (will be shared by Samir).
